assumptions: The seven headline premises (Premises w0 env), as H3.

Explicit hypotheses, not premises: an L1 clock that never runs backwards and queue entries of the landing World that carry their enqueue block's L1 timestamp (these stand in for the L1 clock the model's steps do not carry; the contract records block.timestamp), and accepted anchors that report their own block's timestamp and count every entry enqueued at or before that block (AnchorHonesty.AnchorCovers, a guest obligation: anchors must be authenticated L1 blocks).
theorems.scope: H3's third part against the Inbox's actual queue: a landed block consumes the queue-head entry once it is due by the anchor's time, and 7.3's block-time bound holds (block.timestamp >= entry.timestamp + forcedInclusionDelay + maxAnchorAge implies it is consumed). Blocks in landed segments only; no wall-clock deadline and no liveness.

theorems.type: Etna.Statements.ForcedInclusionIntegrity
assumptions: Etna.Statements.Premises: genesis (the initialized World), verifierSound (two proofs, one sound backend that approves only certified statements), hashSeparation (the stored config commitment's only uint256 opening) and authenticatedInputs (an authenticated FI witness for an index below the anchor's tail, under an authenticated anchor from the current generation's origin L1 block up to, not including, the landing's block shows the World's queue entry); headerHashes, headerSeparation and signatureAgreement are unused here

the queue and FI-head parts hold along every ProtocolState.Trace from the initialized World; the consumption part ranges over runs whose landings the environment submits (Statements.Run); real proof-backend soundness, FI-witness storage proofs below an accepted anchor's tail and Keccak are premises, not proved; no premise requires an accepted anchor to report the actual tail and timestamp, so pending and due are judged against the tail and timestamp an accepted anchor reports (AnchorTail)

only the blocks of each landed segment are constrained: liveness (that a due entry is ever landed), the maxAnchorAge bound on inclusion delay, raw-transaction canonicality and the EL's given-list build (Forced.step's named witness and singleton inputs) are not claimed
theorems.scope: Headline H3: along every protocol trace from the initialized World each step keeps every FI queue entry, except that a governance recovery blanks exactly the entries its fiToClear lists, and a step that does not advance lastCheckpoint never advances the FI head; along every run, each submitted landing settles blocks valid under rules Deployment.build derives on the World it lands on, from the current checkpoint (cursor = head) to the new one, and those blocks consume every entry in [head, new head) through Forced.step inclusions or legal skips whose witnesses show the World's own queue entries, and consume every entry their anchor shows pending and due. Not claimed: that accepted anchors show the Inbox's actual queue; liveness, the inclusion-delay bound or raw-transaction decoding.
